questions.question: Which continent saw its first nation join BRICS as a full member in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Africa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Africa became the first continent to have a new member join BRICS in 2025, marking a significant milestone in global geopolitics.
 
• The nation joining BRICS from Africa was **Egypt**, which officially became a full member in 2025 as part of BRICS expansion efforts.
 
• BRICS, consisting of Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, represents leading emerging economies, with South Africa being the first African country to join in 2010.
 
• Egypt’s inclusion in 2025 highlights Africa's growing influence in the global economic and political landscape.
 
• BRICS aims to promote cooperation among emerging markets, ensuring representation from diverse regions, including Africa, which holds immense potential in resources, trade, and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **South America**:

 
 
• Brazil is the only South American nation in BRICS, which has been a founding member since 2009.
 
• South America plays a critical role in BRICS through Brazil's contributions in agriculture, energy, and regional diplomacy.
 
• While South America has strong economic potential, no additional countries from the continent joined BRICS in 2025.
 
 
 
• **Southeast Asia**:
 
 
• Southeast Asia is represented indirectly through partnerships with BRICS member countries, especially China and India.
 
• Countries like Indonesia and Malaysia have expressed interest in closer cooperation with BRICS but did not join as full members in 2025.
 
• The region remains pivotal for global trade and manufacturing but has not formally entered BRICS membership.
 
 
 
• **Europe**:
 
 
• No European nation has joined BRICS as a member as the bloc focuses on emerging economies outside of the developed Western framework.
 
• Russia is the sole member from Europe, bringing a unique geopolitical perspective to BRICS.
 
• While Europe has a significant global presence, BRICS primarily focuses on economic cooperation among non-Western nations.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Overview**:
 
 
• BRICS stands for Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, established to promote cooperation among leading emerging economies.
 
• It focuses on economic growth, sustainable development, and multipolarity in global politics.
 
• The inclusion of new members like Egypt reflects the bloc's aim to expand representation and enhance its geopolitical influence.

questions.question:
Which of the following countries is NOT listed among BRICS 'partner countries' as of

2025?

The correct answer is __**Argentina**__.

__

• During the **16th BRICS Summit** held in **Kazan, Russia** (October 2024), the bloc officially introduced a new membership category known as **Partner Countries** to expand its influence without immediate full membership.

• As of **2025**, a total of **13 nations** were officially invited and recognized as **BRICS partner countries**. This list includes **Algeria**, **Belarus**, **Bolivia**, **Cuba**, **Indonesia**, **Kazakhstan**, **Malaysia**, **Nigeria**, **Thailand**, **Turkey**, **Uganda**, **Uzbekistan**, and **Vietnam**.

• **Argentina** is not included in this list. Although it was initially invited to become a **full member** during the **15th BRICS Summit** in 2023, the administration of **President Javier Milei** formally withdrew the country's bid and declined the invitation in **December 2023**.

• **Cuba**, **Belarus**, and **Uganda** are all part of the newly established **partner country** framework, which allows them to participate in specific **BRICS** initiatives and meetings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **BRICS Expansion (2024)**:

• The group underwent its most significant expansion on **January 1, 2024**, when **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, and the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** officially became full members.

• **Saudi Arabia** was also invited; however, the kingdom has maintained a cautious approach and has not yet completed the formal joining process as of early 2025.

• **Partner Country Status**:

• This designation was created to handle the surge in interest from over **30 nations** seeking to align with the **BRICS** bloc.

• Partners have access to **New Development Bank (NDB)** projects and high-level **diplomatic dialogues** but lack the **veto power** and voting rights reserved for the **original members** and the 2024 intake.

• **Strategic Shifts**:

• **Argentina's** decision to opt out was driven by a radical shift in **foreign policy** toward closer alignment with the **United States** and **Western economic institutions**.

• The inclusion of **Turkey** as a partner country is particularly notable as it is the first **NATO member** to seek a formal partnership with the **BRICS** group.

</ul

questions.question: Which organisation, in July 2025, formally recognised the pivotal role played by heads of state and government in securing the adoption of the "Pandemic Agreement" in May 2025?

options.text: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Health Organization**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **World Health Organization (WHO)**, in **July 2025**, formally expressed its gratitude and recognition for the **Heads of State and Government** who provided the necessary political momentum to finalize the **Pandemic Agreement**.

• The **Pandemic Agreement** was officially adopted in **May 2025** during the **78th World Health Assembly** held in **Geneva, Switzerland**.

• The recognition highlighted how high-level political involvement was essential to overcome deadlocks in negotiations concerning **equitable access** to medical countermeasures and **pathogen-sharing** mechanisms.

• **Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus**, the **Director-General** of the **WHO**, noted that the agreement represents a **generational pact** to protect future populations from the devastating social and economic impacts of pandemics.

• This milestone marked the culmination of a process that began with a **Special Session** of the **World Health Assembly** in **December 2021**, where Member States agreed to establish an **Intergovernmental Negotiating Body (INB)**.

**Additional Information__**

__

• **The Pandemic Agreement (WHO CA+):**

• It is a legally binding international instrument established under **Article 19** of the **WHO Constitution**, which allows the **World Health Assembly** to adopt conventions or agreements on any matter within the competence of the Organization.

• The primary objective of the agreement is to strengthen **Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness, and Response (PPPR)** by fostering **global cooperation** and transparency.

• Key provisions of the 2025 agreement include the **WHO Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) System** and the **Global Supply Chain and Logistics Network**.

• **World Health Organization (WHO):**

• Founded on **7 April 1948**, the **WHO** is the specialized agency of the **United Nations** responsible for international public health.

• Its headquarters is located in **Geneva, Switzerland**, and it operates through **six regional offices** globally.

• The **World Health Assembly (WHA)** is the supreme decision-making body of the **WHO**, attended by delegations from all **194 Member States**.

• **International Health Regulations (IHR):**

• Parallel to the **Pandemic Agreement**, the **International Health Regulations (2005)** were also targeted for targeted amendments in **2024** and **2025** to improve **early warning systems** and **surveillance**.

• While the **Pandemic Agreement** focuses on long-term equity and structural preparedness, the **IHR** provides the legal framework for responding to **Public Health Emergencies of International Concern (PHEIC)**.

• **Other Organizations Mentioned:**

• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** focuses on global **monetary cooperation** and financial stability, not public health treaties.

• **UNESCO** (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) deals with **education**, **science**, and **culture**.

• The **World Bank** provides **financial and technical assistance** to developing countries, often supporting health projects, but it does not host the **Pandemic Agreement**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Pandemic Agreement** emphasizes the principle of **Sovereignty**, ensuring that **Member States** have the sovereign right to legislate and implement legislation in pursuance of their **public health policies**.

• It addresses the **One Health** approach, recognizing the interconnection between the health of **people, animals, and ecosystems** to prevent zoonotic spillovers.

• The **2025** adoption follows years of intensive diplomatic sessions by the **Intergovernmental Negotiating Body (INB)**, which included **Bureau members** representing different **WHO regions** like **Africa, the Americas, South-East Asia, Europe, Eastern Mediterranean, and Western Pacific**.
</ul

questions.question: According to UNESCO, The World Heritage Cities Programme, the World Heritage Committee inducted two cities Orchha and Gwalior in the UNESCO's World Heritage Cities, is from which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• In **December 2020**, the **United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)** included the historical cities of **Gwalior** and **Orchha** from **Madhya Pradesh** in its **World Heritage Cities Programme**.

• **Gwalior** was established in the **9th century** and has been ruled by various dynasties including the **Gurjar Pratihara Rajvansh**, **Tomars**, **Baghel Kachvaho**, and **Scindias**. It is famous for the **Gwalior Fort**, often described as the 'Gibraltar of India', which houses monuments like the **Man Singh Palace**, **Gujari Mahal**, and **Sas Bahu Temple**.

• **Orchha** was founded in the **16th century** (around **1501 AD**) by **Rudra Pratap Singh** of the **Bundela dynasty**. It served as the capital of the **Bundela kingdom** and is situated on the banks of the **Betwa River**.

• The city of **Orchha** is renowned for its **Bundela architecture**, featuring prominent structures such as the **Jehangir Mahal**, **Raj Mahal**, **Rai Praveen Mahal**, and the **Ram Raja Temple**, which is the only temple in India where **Lord Rama** is worshipped as a king.

• The induction into the **World Heritage Cities Programme** implies that **UNESCO** will collaborate with the state government to create a master plan for the **conservation** and **restoration** of these sites.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Other **UNESCO World Heritage Sites** located in **Madhya Pradesh** include:

• **Khajuraho Group of Monuments**: Recognized in **1986** for its intricate **Nagara-style** temples and sculptures.

• **Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi**: Inscribed in **1989**, it is one of the oldest stone structures in India, established by **Emperor Ashoka**.

• **Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka**: Inscribed in **2003**, featuring cave paintings dating back to the **Paleolithic** and **Mesolithic** periods.

• The **World Heritage Cities Programme** is a global initiative aimed at assisting state parties in the **protection** and **management** of their **urban heritage**.
</ul

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding OPEC:

 
• All member countries of OPEC are also members of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
 
• OPEC coordinates and unifies petroleum policies among its member countries.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries)** was founded in **1960** in **Baghdad, Iraq** by **Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela**; its members are mainly major oil-exporting developing economies, not OECD countries.
 
• The **OECD (Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development)** consists primarily of developed economies such as the **United States, United Kingdom, Japan, Germany and France**; most OPEC members are not OECD members, therefore the first statement does not hold.
 
• OPEC’s core objective is to **coordinate and unify petroleum policies** among member countries to ensure **stable oil markets**, fair returns to producers and regular supply to consumers.
 
• OPEC decisions regarding **crude oil production levels** are taken during Ministerial Meetings and directly influence global oil prices.
 
• The headquarters of **OPEC** is located in **Vienna, Austria**, and the current Secretary General (as of **2026**) is **Haitham Al Ghais**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries)**

 
 
• Established in **1960**; headquarters at **Vienna, Austria**.
 
• As of **2026**, OPEC has **12 member countries** including Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, UAE, Kuwait and Venezuela.
 
• The **OPEC+ alliance** includes non-OPEC producers like **Russia** to coordinate global oil production.
 
• OPEC meetings determine output adjustments to manage price volatility.
 
 
 
• **Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)**
 
 
• Established in **1961**; headquarters at **Paris, France**.
 
• OECD currently has **38 member countries** (as of 2026).
 
• It publishes the **OECD Economic Outlook** report.
 
• OECD members are mostly high-income developed economies.
 
 
 
• **International Energy Agency (IEA)**
 
 
• Established in **1974** in response to the oil crisis.
 
• Headquarters located in **Paris, France**.
 
• IEA works closely with OECD countries on energy security.
 
• Publishes the **World Energy Outlook** annually.

questions.question: Who is the current President of president of World Trade Organization (WTO)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala** is the current Director-General of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**. She took office on **March 1, 2021**, making history as the first woman and the first African to lead the WTO.
 
• Her appointment as the Director-General came after a comprehensive selection process and unanimous support from member countries.
 
• Born on **June 13, 1954**, in **Nigeria**, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is an economist and international development expert with over 30 years of experience in global financial institutions.
 
• She has previously served as the **Finance Minister of Nigeria** and as the Managing Director of the **World Bank**, where she handled development projects and policies worldwide.
 
• As the WTO chief, Okonjo-Iweala focuses on critical issues such as **trade policy reforms**, addressing global trade inequalities, and revitalizing the WTO's dispute resolution mechanisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO):**

 
 
• The WTO was established on **January 1, 1995**, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) that had been in place since 1948.
 
• It is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**, and is responsible for regulating international trade, ensuring smooth trade flows, and resolving trade disputes between member nations.
 
• The WTO has **164 member countries**, representing over 98% of global trade, making it one of the most comprehensive international trade organizations.
 
 
 
• **Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala’s Achievements:**
 
 
• She spearheaded reforms in Nigeria's public financial systems, introducing **transparency and accountability** measures during her tenure as Finance Minister.
 
• She was instrumental in negotiating **Nigeria’s debt relief**, securing a debt write-off of $18 billion and a reduction of Nigeria’s debt stock by $30 billion with the Paris Club in 2005.
 
• She has been recognized globally, appearing on **Forbes' list of 100 Most Powerful Women** and receiving honorary degrees from prestigious universities.
 
 
 
• **Challenges at the WTO:**
 
 
• The WTO faces criticism for its inability to resolve long-standing trade disputes, such as those between **the United States and China**.
 
• Reforming its **Appellate Body** and dispute resolution mechanism is a key priority under Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala’s leadership.
 
• Addressing the inequitable distribution of vaccines and ensuring fair trade practices amid the COVID-19 pandemic are also major challenges.
 
 
 
• **Significance of WTO Leadership:**
 
 
• As the first African to lead the WTO, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala brings a unique perspective on trade issues affecting **developing countries**.
 
• Her leadership is expected to bridge the gap between **developed and developing nations**, ensuring inclusive trade policies that benefit all member countries.
 
• She has emphasized the importance of **trade as a tool for economic recovery** and poverty alleviation globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility Criteria for WTO Leadership:**

 
 
• The selection process for the Director-General is based on **consensus among member nations**.
 
• Candidates must have extensive experience in **international trade, economics, or public service**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the WTO Director-General:**
 
 
• The Director-General is responsible for providing **strategic direction** to the organization and ensuring smooth functioning of its operations.
 
• The position involves mediating trade negotiations and resolving disputes among member countries.
 
 
 
• **Notable Past Directors-General:**
 
 
• **Pascal Lamy** (2005–2013) from France, focused on trade liberalization.
 
• **Roberto Azevêdo** (2013–2020) from Brazil, emphasized WTO reforms.

questions.question: How many members voted in favour of the IAEA resolution declaring Iran non-compliant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__19__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) passed a resolution declaring Iran non-compliant with its obligations under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).
 
• The resolution was adopted by a majority vote, with 19 out of 35 members of the IAEA Board of Governors voting in favor.
 
• In favor (19): Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Canada, Colombia, Ecuador, France, Georgia, Germany, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Morocco, the Netherlands, South Korea, Spain, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
 
• Against (3): China, Russia, and Burkina Faso (Niger voted against in the November 2025 resolution).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA):**

 
 
• IAEA is an independent organization established in 1957 to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy and prevent nuclear weapons proliferation.
 
• It works under the framework of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), conducting inspections and monitoring activities to ensure compliance.
 
• The IAEA Board of Governors comprises 35 member states, which play a crucial role in decision-making on nuclear safety and compliance.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT):**
 
 
• The NPT is a landmark international treaty aimed at preventing the spread of nuclear weapons and promoting peaceful nuclear energy uses.
 
• It was opened for signature in 1968 and entered into force in 1970, with over 190 parties as signatories.
 
• It is based on three pillars: nuclear disarmament, non-proliferation, and the peaceful use of nuclear energy.
 
 
 
• **Iran’s Nuclear Program:**
 
 
• Iran’s nuclear program has been under scrutiny due to suspicions of its development of nuclear weapons, despite its claims of peaceful intentions.
 
• The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), signed in 2015, was a significant effort to limit Iran’s nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief.

questions.question:
Which of the following countries are members of the European Union ?

1. Belarus

2. Poland

3. Germany

4. Switzerland

Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Belarus** is a landlocked country in **Eastern Europe** that is not a member of the **European Union**. It maintains close political and economic ties with **Russia** via the **Union State** and has never applied for EU membership. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Poland** joined the **European Union** on **May 1, 2004**, during the largest single wave of enlargement in the union's history. It is a significant political member and participates in the **Schengen Area**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Germany** is one of the six **founding members** of the **European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC)** in 1951 and the **European Economic Community (EEC)** in 1957. It remains a central economic and political pillar of the current **European Union**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Switzerland** is not a member of the **European Union**. Although it is integrated into the **European Single Market** and the **Schengen Area** through various **bilateral agreements**, it maintains its sovereignty and has withdrawn its application for membership. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The European Union (EU)**:

 
 
• It is an international organization comprising **27 European countries** governing common economic, social, and security policies.
 
• The **Maastricht Treaty**, which took effect in **1993**, is the foundation for the modern EU and the creation of the **Euro** currency.
 
• The **European Parliament**, **European Council**, and **European Commission** are the primary decision-making bodies located mostly in **Brussels**, **Luxembourg**, and **Strasbourg**.
 
 
 
• **EFTA and Non-Members**:
 
 
• The **European Free Trade Association (EFTA)** includes **Iceland**, **Liechtenstein**, **Norway**, and **Switzerland**. These nations are not in the EU but trade extensively with it.
 
• The **United Kingdom** is the only sovereign country to have left the union, a process known as **Brexit**, completed on **January 31, 2020**.

questions.question: This organization has Gita Gopinath as the Chief Economist. Where is the headquarters of this organization situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Washington DC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gita Gopinath** serves as the **Chief Economist** of the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**. She assumed this position in **October 2018**, becoming the first woman to occupy this role.
 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** is an international organization established in **1944** at the Bretton Woods Conference to promote global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, and facilitate international trade.
 
• The headquarters of the **IMF** is located in **Washington DC, United States**, making it a pivotal location for global economic decision-making.
 
• The choice of Washington DC as the headquarters aligns with the fact that the IMF operates closely with the **World Bank**, which is also headquartered in Washington DC.
 
• The IMF's governance includes **190 member countries**, each working towards global economic stability, poverty reduction, and sustainable growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF):**

 
 
• The IMF was formally established on **December 27, 1945**, and its operational headquarters are located at **700 19th Street NW, Washington DC**.
 
• The organization provides **financial assistance** and advice to member countries facing economic crises, such as balance-of-payment deficits.
 
• The IMF is responsible for overseeing the **global monetary system** and ensuring the stability of exchange rates and international payments.
 
• It also offers technical assistance and training to member countries in areas like fiscal policies, monetary policies, and exchange rate management.
 
 
 
• **Gita Gopinath:**
 
 
• She is an Indian-American economist who has contributed significantly to the field of **macroeconomics** and international finance.
 
• Before joining the IMF, she was the **John Zwaanstra Professor of International Studies and Economics** at Harvard University.
 
• Her work focuses on currency movements, trade policies, and international capital flows.
 
 
 
• **Other Global Economic Institutions:**
 
 
• **World Bank:** Headquarters are also in **Washington DC**, focusing on long-term economic development and poverty reduction.
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO):** Headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**, it deals with trade rules among nations.
 
• **United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD):** Headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**, focusing on trade, investment, and development issues.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IMF Membership:**

 
 
• The IMF has **190 member countries**, and each contributes financial resources to the organization.
 
• Members have voting rights based on their financial contributions, known as **quotas**.
 
 
 
• **IMF Programs:**
 
 
• The IMF undertakes programs such as **Structural Adjustment** to help countries stabilize their economies.
 
• It conducts regular economic analysis and publishes reports like the **World Economic Outlook** and **Global Financial Stability Report**.
 
 
 
• **Washington DC:**
 
 
• Washington DC is the capital city of the **United States** and home to several international organizations, including the IMF and World Bank.
 
• It is a major center for economic policymaking and global diplomacy.

questions.question: Which option best reflects India’s diplomatic and operational stance on India–Myanmar boundary demarcation amid recent protests?

options.text: Arbitration through BIMSTEC under a 1987 treaty
Joint surveys and proposal of a Joint Boundary Working Group
Suspension of fencing to protect ASEAN trade
Complete dismissal of protests under AFSPA

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joint surveys and proposal of a Joint Boundary Working Group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India’s approach to **boundary demarcation with Myanmar** is centered on **diplomatic collaboration**, ensuring stability and addressing concerns from both sides.
 
• **Joint surveys** are conducted to ensure accurate mapping of the boundary line, taking into account geographical, ethnic, and administrative considerations. This ensures the process is transparent and acceptable to both nations.
 
• The establishment of a **Joint Boundary Working Group** facilitates bilateral discussions and ensures that the demarcation process is mutually agreed upon without conflict. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• India’s stance avoids unilateral actions like suspension of fencing or dismissing protests under laws like **AFSPA**. Instead, it focuses on dialogue and collaboration.
 
• The **Joint Boundary Working Group** also addresses concerns raised by local communities, ensuring their grievances are considered while demarcating boundaries.
 
• This approach reflects India's commitment to maintaining **peaceful relations** with Myanmar and ensuring that operational and diplomatic strategies align with regional stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India–Myanmar Boundary:**

 
 
• The **India–Myanmar boundary** spans approximately **1,643 km** and traverses regions like Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram.
 
• This boundary is characterized by **ethnic diversity**, with several tribes and communities residing along its length.
 
 
 
• **Joint Boundary Working Group:**
 
 
• The Joint Boundary Working Group is a **bilateral mechanism** aimed at resolving boundary-related issues and ensuring **mutual cooperation**.
 
• It facilitates **joint surveys**, ensuring that both nations collaborate in the demarcation process to prevent disputes.
 
• **Example:** The group has been instrumental in resolving disputes in areas like the Indo-Myanmar Friendship Road region.

questions.question: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure body is associated with which of the following International Organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shanghai Cooperation Organisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS)** is a permanent organ of the **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)**, which is focused on addressing terrorism, separatism, and extremism in the region.
 
• The headquarters of RATS is located in **Tashkent, Uzbekistan**, and it plays a pivotal role in fostering regional cooperation on security matters.
 
• RATS promotes intelligence sharing, joint counter-terrorism exercises, and the coordination of operations between member states to combat transnational threats.
 
• SCO, established in **2001**, is an intergovernmental organization that primarily aims to enhance political, economic, and security cooperation among its members, which include countries like **China, Russia, India, Pakistan**, and others.
 
• Through RATS, SCO member states work together to counter issues such as terrorist financing, cyberterrorism, and the proliferation of extremist ideologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO):**

 
 
• The SCO is a political, economic, and security alliance originally founded by **China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan** in **2001**. It later expanded to include **India** and **Pakistan** in **2017**.
 
• SCO's goals include promoting peace, stability, and development in the region, as well as combating terrorism, drug trafficking, and organized crime.
 
• It is considered one of the world's largest regional organizations, covering a significant portion of the Eurasian continent.
 
 
 
• **RATS Structure and Functions:**
 
 
• RATS acts as a coordination center for member states to combat terrorism, separatism, and extremism.
 
• It facilitates regular meetings, the exchange of intelligence, and the development of joint strategies to counter regional security challenges.
 
• RATS also focuses on issues related to cybersecurity, such as addressing cyberterrorism and ensuring safe digital communication.
 
 
 
• **Key SCO Initiatives:**
 
 
• Joint military exercises such as the **“Peace Mission”** drills, aimed at strengthening counter-terrorism capabilities.
 
• Promotion of regional economic connectivity through initiatives like the **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)** and regional trade agreements.
 
• Cultural and educational exchanges to foster mutual understanding and cooperation among member states.
 
 
 
• **Important Points about Other Options:**
 
 
• **BRICS:** A group of five major emerging economies – Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa – focused on economic cooperation and development but not directly associated with RATS.
 
• **Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC):** Comprises 57 member states and is focused on promoting solidarity among Islamic countries; it does not have a specific anti-terror body like RATS.
 
• **SAARC:** The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation aims to promote development and cooperation in South Asia but has no direct affiliation with RATS.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SCO Member States:** The organization consists of eight permanent members: China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. Observer states include Iran, Afghanistan, Belarus, and Mongolia.
 
• **RATS Achievements:** RATS has contributed to enhancing regional security through intelligence sharing, capacity building, and joint counter-terrorism operations.
 
• **Significance of SCO:** With its focus on security and economic integration, SCO plays a critical role in stabilizing Central Asia and fostering cooperation between Eurasian nations.
 
• **Challenges:** Despite its achievements, SCO faces challenges such as differing political ideologies among members and the complex geopolitical environment of the region.
